status: diagnostic phase complete; candidate implementation and model calls paused per latest user direction
direct_observations: GPT used one batched read response per round (11, 7, 6 read_sheet calls), then one batched write response (Decisions, four Summary cells, report), separate save, then advance/finish.

The three audited task variants completed in 10/10/14 requests and 29/29/49 tools, each with zero invalid actions and no retries. The observed request pattern is 4 times number of rounds plus 2; this describes these traces only.
read_sheet returns the whole named sheet. list_sheets exposes all sheets. write_decisions replaces the full decision table in one call.
Commitments re-exposes prior accepted IDs and locked amounts. receive_update explicitly lists changed sheets. Relevant history can be reconstructed from the current workbook.

Updates happen only through receive_update after a correct saved delivery. There are no observed concurrent changes between read and save, ambiguous side-effect outcomes, or rollback/reconciliation branches.
Actual model-facing tools offered no general Python/code execution or arithmetic solver; GPT did not use an external solver tool or access hidden reference answers in the recorded trajectory.
supported_inferences: The current family is mainly a fully observed deterministic computation repeated behind stage gates. It does not require remembering hidden historical state: current sheets encode that state.
Batch interfaces reduce row count and rule additions to larger message contents, rather than necessarily creating more interaction or exploration decisions.
GPT did not evade stated requirements; it used a permitted low-interaction workflow. Making snapshots harder to read solely to force more calls would not by itself improve benchmark validity.
Qwen failures here establish weaknesses in these specific bounded tasks (calculation, eligibility, ordering, saving and artifact consistency), but are not a validated predictor of GPT difficulty.
Qwen screening remains useful for harness diagnostics and reproducible model-specific failures. It should not alone be treated as proof that a task warrants paid GPT testing.
